newsitem.title: USA: Minorca faces class-action suit - lawyers.
newsitem.headline: Minorca faces class-action suit - lawyers.

text.p: A class-action lawsuit was filed against Minorca Resources Inc on behalf of investors who bought special warrants in the company through a private placement, attorneys for the plaintiffs said Thursday.
The complaint alleges that Minorca made misrepresentations about gold resource calculations made for the Busang deposit in the Indonesian province of Kalimantan.
Minorca officials was not immediately available for comment.
The complaint charges that Minorca "blindly" relied upon gold resource calculations that were derived from sample-testing methods not generally accepted by the industry.
The suit alleges that after the closing of the special warrants offer on March 13, sample testing using industry-accepted methods showed insignificant amounts of gold at the Busang deposit.
Immediately after the initial disclosure of the overstated calculations, the price of Minorca common stock dropped about 70 percent, the complaint says.
Minorca Resources Inc, Scotia McLeod Inc, and Scotia Capital Markets Inc are named in the suit, which was filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.
The offering of special warrants was conducted through a syndicate of seven underwriters, including Scotia McLeod Inc and Scotia Capital Markets Inc.
The complaint seeks damages and rescinding of the warrant offer on behalf of the class.
The plaintiff, Arthur Abbey, is represented by Curtis Trinko LLP.
